primitives.name: Dynamic Bradley-Terry Strength Estimator
primitives.verbatim_quote: ### 2109.13743v2.pdf - Method: extends the Bradley-Terry pairwise-strength model to comparisons whose probabilities drift over time, estimating strengths from a sliding neighborhood of recent comparisons.
primitives.assumptions: Pairwise comparison probabilities follow Bradley-Terry form, strengths evolve within a fixed-time window.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When recent window lacks sufficient comparisons or when strength drift exceeds model capacity.

layer2.mapping: Strength estimates derived from sliding-window pairwise outcomes enable dynamic rating updates and temporal consistency checks.
layer2.telemetry: Sliding window size, strength variance, convergence rate

reasoning_traces.think:
The core operators derive from probabilistic modeling frameworks—logistic regression for binary outcomes and Bradley-Terry for pairwise comparisons. These models are unified under a common theme of directional inference from structured data. Logistic regression provides calibrated probability estimates for win/loss outcomes given game features, while Bradley-Terry models capture relative team strength dynamics. The dynamic extension allows for temporal evolution of these strengths, aligning with GSE’s need for evolving ratings. Bias correction enhances the reliability of strength gaps, ensuring that directional premises are grounded in empirical validation rather than mere statistical fit. Failure modes include overfitting in logistic models due to sparse feature spaces and instability in strength estimation when recent comparison windows are too small or noisy.
